boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all ten frozen records in the Gettysburg Campaign [June-July 1863]. Preserve per-engagement dates. Middleburg (June 17–19) overlaps Aldie (June 17), and Boonsboro (July 8) lies inside Williamsport's frozen interval (July 6–16); campaign-wide and multi-day totals (for example Stuart's June 17–21 losses and the Count of Paris's campaign estimates) must not be assigned to one engagement or added. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen structured bounds (US 7,000; CS 12,500) are imported source-reported figures and remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force text reads 19,500 total (US 7,000; CS 12,500), with matching structured bounds, and the live field agrees. Doubleday calls Milroy's garrison very considerable and says a prisoner told Milroy he faced Ewell's corps; Lee says more than 2,300 infantry surrendered to Johnson, more than the force Johnson engaged.
claims.rationale: Imported bounds are unchanged; the report figures are not opening strengths.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty texts read 4,709 total (US 4,443; CS 266). Lee gives the Confederate loss as 47 killed, 219 wounded and 3 missing, and 4,000 prisoners taken in all the Valley operations. Doubleday relays Milroy's claim to have brought off 5,000 men, Early's 3,358 prisoners sent to Richmond and Johnson's 2,800.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Lee's totals include Martinsburg and other Valley operations; prisoner counts differ by reporter.

open_questions: Ewell's, Early's, Johnson's and Milroy's reports and the Winchester court of inquiry remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Doubleday is an interested participant history (he commanded the First Corps at Gettysburg) and Humphreys an interested history by Meade's later chief of staff; both drew on official papers. Lee's and Stuart's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXVII, Part 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
